title: Autonomous agents: what runs an agent when no one is in the conversation?
summary: Hold: the capacity-enforcement explanation omits an important exception. An environment with remaining allocated prepaid credits can keep running even when tenant consumption reaches 125%; the documented trigger, authentication and sharing controls otherwise support the page.

claims.claim: An autonomous Copilot Studio agent acts on an event rather than waiting for a user prompt.
claims.quote: Unlike topic triggers, which require input from a user, event triggers allow an agent to act autonomously in response to the specified event.

claims.claim: Event-driven execution does not mean the agent runs continuously.
claims.quote: Event-driven execution doesn't mean the agent runs continuously.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Creation of a SharePoint item can trigger an agent.
claims.quote: When an item is created in SharePoint

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Completion of a Planner task can trigger an agent.
claims.quote: When a task is completed in Planner

claims.where: summary; What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A Recurrence trigger can start an agent after a set time.
claims.quote: A set amount of time passed (a **Recurrence** trigger)

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: An event trigger sends a trigger payload to the agent through a connector.
claims.quote: Event triggers require a chosen event that generates a *trigger payload* and sends it to the agent through a connector.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The agent follows the author's instructions and instructions sent in the payload.
claims.quote: When the agent receives the payload, it executes the directions provided by the agent author in the agent's instructions and instructions sent through the trigger payload.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The author defines the actions or topics the agent can select.
claims.quote: Your agent doesn't create a new action or topic on the spot. As the agent author, you need to define the actions or topics it can select from.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Standard-harness event triggers require generative orchestration.
claims.quote: This feature is only available for agents with generative orchestration turned on.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Publishing starts it
claims.claim: A standard-harness agent does not react automatically to a new trigger before publication.
claims.quote: Before you publish your agent with a new event trigger, the agent doesn't automatically react to that trigger.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Publishing starts it
claims.claim: After publication with a new trigger, a standard-harness agent reacts automatically each time the trigger activates.
claims.quote: after you publish an agent with a new trigger, your agent reacts automatically each time its triggers are activated.

claims.claim: The Activity page records the standard-harness agent's triggers and reactions.
claims.quote: You can see a step-by-step record of your agent's triggers and reactions in the Activity page.

claims.where: What it is: Microsoft Copilot harness preview activation
claims.claim: In the Microsoft Copilot harness preview, Activate for me opens Agent management, where the maker turns on the agent.
claims.quote: **Activate for me** takes you to **Agent management**, where you turn on the agent.

claims.where: What it is: Microsoft Copilot harness preview activation
claims.claim: Turning on the preview agent starts it running on the maker's behalf.
claims.quote: After you turn on the agent, your agent starts running on your behalf.

claims.where: What it is: authentication table; Why it matters; Risks and limits: Author credentials reach every user
claims.claim: Standard-harness event triggers can authenticate only with the agent author's credentials.
claims.quote: Currently, event triggers can use only the agent author's credentials for authentication.

claims.claim: After publishing a Microsoft Copilot harness preview agent, the maker can activate it for themselves using maker credentials or share it.
claims.quote: **Activate for myself**: Only you, the maker, can use the agent, using your own maker credentials.

claims.claim: Recipients of a shared preview autonomous agent use their own credentials.
claims.quote: **Share with others**: Allow other users use the agent, with their own credentials.

claims.claim: Each recipient sets up required connections on the agent management page.
claims.quote: use the *agent management* page to connect required services with your own credentials, configure the trigger settings that the agent owner allows, and turn triggers on or off.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends explicit permissions, decision boundaries and human oversight for autonomous agents.
claims.quote: Design autonomy around explicit permissions, decision boundaries, and human oversight.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to rely on instructions alone to prevent unauthorized actions.
claims.quote: Don't rely on instructions, such as "only send an email after checking a knowledge source," to prevent unauthorized actions.

claims.claim: A Recurrence trigger configured for every 10 minutes sends a payload every 10 minutes.
claims.quote: a recurrence trigger set to activate every 10 minutes sends a trigger payload to the agent every 10 minutes.

claims.claim: Agent makers can add event triggers to agents.
claims.quote: Agent makers in your organization can add event triggers to agents.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].governs; Why it matters; What to check; Open questions
claims.claim: A data policy blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector prevents makers from adding event triggers.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers to their agents or running automated evaluations by using an authenticated account, configure a data policy that blocks the **Microsoft Copilot Studio** connector.

claims.claim: Standard-harness event trigger activity consumes Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Event trigger activity counts toward Copilot Credit consumption.

claims.claim: Each trigger payload is processed like a user message and the response is billed at the Copilot Credits billing rates.
claims.quote: Each trigger payload that an event trigger sends to an agent is processed like a message from a user, and the agent's response is billed at the Copilot Credits billing rates.

claims.claim: Trigger steps count as agent actions in the standard-harness billing definitions.
claims.quote: Agent actions refer to steps such as triggers, deep reasoning, and topic transitions that appear on the activity map in Copilot Studio when testing an agent.

claims.claim: The standard agent-action billing rate is 5 Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: | Agent action^4^ | 5 Copilot Credits | No charge |

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness charges Copilot Credits for LLM tokens, tools including knowledge and MCPs, and the harness itself.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Microsoft 365 Copilot licence
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot agent-flow no-charge exemption does not apply when the agent runs autonomously.
claims.quote: This exemption doesn't apply when the agent runs autonomously, for example after an event trigger or a Power Automate flow starts it.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Microsoft 365 Copilot licence
claims.claim: Agent flows called by autonomous agents consume credits and are subject to enforcement even when users have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses.
claims.quote: Agent flow runs called by an autonomous agent consume Copilot Credits and are subject to enforcement, even if the users in your organization have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses.

claims.claim: The prepaid capacity enforcement policy includes autonomously triggered custom-agent usage.
claims.quote: Applies to all tenants operating under the Copilot Studio prepaid capacity model for custom agent usage (conversational and autonomously triggered).

claims.claim: Tenant prepaid capacity enforcement is triggered at 125% of prepaid capacity.
claims.quote: Enforcement is triggered when a tenant reaches 125% of their prepaid capacity.

claims.claim: Reaching the tenant's 125% prepaid-capacity threshold blocks the environment's agents, with only pay-as-you-go given as an exception.
claims.quote: If the tenant is already at 125% Copilot Credit consumption because of Environment B and Environment C, enforcement isn't placed on the agents in Environment A, as long as Environment A has remaining capacity from its allocation of 10,000 Copilot Credits.
claims.fix: After the sentence about enforcement blocking the environment's agents, add: 'An environment with remaining allocated prepaid capacity is not blocked by the tenant reaching 125% while that allocation remains available.' This qualification is documented in the Enforcement example at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management#enforcement-example.

claims.claim: An environment billing overage to pay-as-you-go is not blocked by exhaustion of prepaid credits.
claims.quote: If an environment bills overage to a pay-as-you-go plan, running out of prepaid Copilot Credits doesn't block the agents in that environment, and usage that prepaid capacity doesn't cover is billed to the plan.

claims.claim: Each recipient's preview autonomous-agent usage is totaled and billed through the hosting environment.
claims.quote: Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the underlying environment where the agent is hosted.

claims.claim: The event trigger overview states no separate autonomous-agent-specific license.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio event triggers autonomous agents separate license licensing prerequisites'; read authoring-triggers-about and billing-licensing in full. The overview documents credits and orchestration, not a separate autonomous-agent license.

claims.claim: General authoring-access requirements are documented in Licensing for agents powered by the standard harness.
claims.quote: To use Copilot Studio, you need one of the following configurations:

claims.where: Risks and limits: Author credentials reach every user; Why it matters
claims.claim: Users of an agent with authenticated standard-harness triggers might access information or prompt actions using the author's credentials.
claims.quote: If you publish an agent with authenticated event triggers, users might access information or prompt the agent to perform actions by using the author's credentials.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Payloads can leak
claims.claim: Payloads can contain sensitive information that the agent outputs elsewhere through actions.
claims.quote: Trigger payloads can potentially contain sensitive information that an agent can output in other locations through actions.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Frequent triggers cost and throttle
claims.claim: Overly frequent triggers can exceed service quotas and cause throttling.
claims.quote: Your agent might then exceed service load quota limits, and your service could be throttled.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Frequent triggers cost and throttle
claims.claim: Shorter trigger intervals use more resources.
claims.quote: The smaller the amount of time between activations, the more resources the trigger uses.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends checking trigger authenticity, including email sender validation.
claims.quote: Ensure that the events or data triggering the agent are authentic and expected. For example, if an agent reacts to incoming emails, use verification checks (like sender validation or specific keywords) so that an attacker can't easily spoof a trigger.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Capacity exhaustion stops agents
claims.claim: An agent that is blocked by capacity enforcement stops responding, including during an existing conversation.
claims.quote: A blocked agent stops responding, including in a conversation that's already in progress.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Capacity exhaustion stops agents
claims.claim: New agent flow runs are blocked separately from agents.
claims.quote: Agent flow runs are blocked separately from agents. New agent flow runs can be blocked while the agent keeps answering questions that don't need a flow.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risks and limits: Triggers need flow sharing; What to check
claims.claim: Adding event triggers requires solution-aware cloud flow sharing to be enabled in the environment.
claims.quote: You can add event triggers to agents only in environments where solution-aware cloud flow sharing is turned on.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risks and limits: Blocking one connector has a second effect
claims.claim: Blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector also prevents automated evaluations using authenticated accounts.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers to their agents or running automated evaluations by using an authenticated account, configure a data policy that blocks the **Microsoft Copilot Studio** connector.

claims.claim: Shared preview autonomous agents do not support workflows that use maker-only credentials.
claims.quote: Workflows that use any maker-only credentials aren't supported for autonomous agents.

claims.claim: Recipients of a shared preview autonomous agent cannot specify or modify tool parameters.
claims.quote: Users of a shared autonomous agent can't specify or modify tool parameters.

claims.claim: Recipients receive no notification when a maker shares an agent with them.
claims.quote: Users don't receive a notification when a maker shares an agent with them.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center data-policy path leads to blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.
claims.quote:
Select the three dots (**⋮**) next to the connector, and then:

    - To prevent agent makers from using the features associated with the connector, select **Block**.
claims.fix: In the front matter and rendered control table, replace the path with 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Add an environment > Available > environment > Add to policy > Assign connectors > Microsoft Copilot Studio > three dots next to the connector > Block'. The printed steps are correct; the omitted more-options button is a minor path omission under the verification standard.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <PolicyGuid> -Classification Blocked -Connectors <ConnectorObjects> classifies the specified connectors as blocked in the target policy.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: The sharing control is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > managed environment > Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing > Let people share solution-aware cloud flows.
claims.quote:
On the **Environments** page, select a managed environment.
5. In the command bar, **Edit Managed Environments**.
6. The sharing rules are located in the **Manage sharing** section.

claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration with EnvironmentName and UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration saves the sharing configuration.
claims.quote: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration

claims.claim: The data policy can govern agents within the environments in its scope.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.where: controls[1].scope and note; Governance controls: Sharing rule
claims.claim: The solution-aware flow and agent-flow sharing rule is an environment-level Managed Environments control.
claims.quote: In managed environments, admins can limit how broadly users can share canvas apps, flows, and agents.

claims.claim: The solutionCloudFlows-limitSharingMode extended setting uses disableSharing to turn off sharing.
claims.quote: $governanceConfiguration.settings.extendedSettings | Add-Member -MemberType NoteProperty -Name 'solutionCloudFlows-limitSharingMode' -Value "disableSharing" -Force

claims.claim: The data-policy prerequisites require a tenant admin or the Environment Admin role.
claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.claim: A tenant-scope data policy applies to all agents in all environments across the tenant.
claims.quote: Policies with a tenant scope apply to all agents in all environments across the tenant.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio enforces data policies in real time.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio supports data policy enforcement in real time.

claims.claim: An enforced event-trigger restriction produces a detailed error in Triggers on the agent's Overview page.
claims.quote: If the policy is enforced, a detailed error message appears in the **Triggers** section on the **Overview** page.

claims.claim: Sharing rules are enforced when users try to share.
claims.quote: Sharing rules are enforced when users try to share an app, flow, or agent.

claims.claim: Sharing rules can take up to an hour to start being enforced.
claims.quote: After sharing rules are set in the Power Platform admin center, it may take up to an hour for them to start getting enforced.

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio Monitor page reports run outcomes for agents with event triggers.
claims.quote: The **Run outcomes** section shows a chart that tracks the type of outcome for each session.

claims.claim: The Monitor page reports trigger use.
claims.quote: The **Trigger use** section shows a chart and metrics that track how often each trigger initiated a session.

claims.claim: The Monitor page reports tool use.
claims.quote: The **Tool use** section shows a chart and metrics that track how often your tools start over time, and how often your agent uses those tools successfully.

claims.claim: The Monitor page reports knowledge source use.
claims.quote: **Knowledge source use**: Learning how often individual knowledge sources are used and how often the agent returned errors.

claims.claim: Monitor analytics can show sessions from the last 360 days.
claims.quote: You can view analytics for sessions that occurred in the last 360 days.

claims.claim: Administrators can monitor resource usage through Power Platform.
claims.quote: Administrators can monitor resource usage through Power Platform.

claims.claim: The pages read do not identify an audit-log event for a trigger-started autonomous-agent run.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio autonomous event trigger audit log unified audit events trigger started'; opened authoring-triggers-about and analytics-improve-agent-health; read Purview audit-copilot and audit-log-activities search excerpts. None identifies a trigger-started run event.

claims.claim: Administrators can govern whether maker-credential connections may be shared for others to use.
claims.quote: Administrators can use the **Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials** setting in the Power Platform admin center to prevent agents from being shared when they contain connections configured to use maker credentials that other users aren't permitted to reuse.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spending policies link; summary
claims.claim: Spending policies control access to supported credit-consuming experiences and how much they can consume.
claims.quote: Use spending policies in the Cost Management dashboard to control access and Copilot Credit spending for AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits and https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-studio-costs to sources for the spending-policy reference. The latter documents Copilot Studio resource-based policies and their precedence over identity-based policies and Power Platform capacity controls.

claims.claim: Let people share solution-aware cloud flows governs sharing of both solution-aware cloud flows and agent flows with individuals and security groups.
claims.quote: **When selected:** Users can share solution-aware cloud flows and agent flows with any number of individuals or security groups. **When not selected:** Users can't share their cloud flows or agent flows with any individual or security group.
